age.evidence: Healthy nulliparous female Wistar rats aged between 9 and 12 weeks

sex.evidence: This study was conducted with female rats

dosing.doses_raw: 15X (4.5 mg/kg bw DMT) and 30X (9 mg/kg bw DMT); acute toxicity also tested at 30X and 50X (15.1 mg/kg bw DMT)
dosing.evidence: Female rats (223 ± 16g) were treated once at 15X (4.5mg/kg bw DMT) and 30X (9mg/kg bw DMT) doses ... administered by oral gavage to the rats

group_housing.evidence: Subjects were kept individually in polypropylene cages under controlled conditions

day_night_flipped.evidence: 12 h/12 h, light/dark; phase direction not stated

assays.assay_description: 96 cm diameter circular white wooden arena with 34 cm wall, floor divided into 18 squares and a central area; 5 min observation 1 h post-dosing. Measured locomotion (quadrants crossed), central entries, rearing, grooming, defecation, urination.

setup_restrain.evidence: animals were placed in the central area and their behaviour observed for 5 min

food_restriction.evidence: Animals were fasted for 12 h prior to gavage, but with free access to water, and food was re-introduced 4 h after dosing

water_restriction.evidence: free access to water in home cage; no water in apparatus during the 5 min test

time_to_assay.evidence: The tests were performed one hour after dosing

sample_size.evidence: n =10 at each dose; fluoxetine positive control group (n =10)

outcomes.summary: Ayahuasca (15X and 30X) and fluoxetine significantly decreased locomotion and rearing compared to controls. Ayahuasca also significantly decreased grooming. Central area entries were reduced but not significantly.
outcomes.evidence: there was a significant decrease in locomotion [F(3.36) = 13.3, P =0.000] and rearing [F(3.36) = 23.8, P =0.000] performed by animals from the fluoxetine and ayahuasca treated groups compared with the controls

B1_num_measures.evidence: locomotion (number of quadrants crossed), number of entries in the central square, and number of rearing, grooming, defecation (number of faecal boli), and urination

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: observed for 5 min; reported as totals

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: no analysis of behavioural sequences reported

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Each test was performed by a trained person, blind to the treatment doses

B8_multivariate.evidence: one-way ANOVA on each measure separately

E1_environment_type.evidence: 96 cm diameter circular white wooden arena

E7_social_context.evidence: focal animal placed alone in arena

E8_food_water.evidence: no food/water in the apparatus during the 5 min test

D1_continuity.evidence: behaviour observed for 5 min on one day

D3_recording_days.evidence: tests performed one hour after dosing, single day

D5_followup.evidence: tests performed 1 h after dosing only

assays.assay_description: Plus-shaped wooden apparatus with two open and two closed arms (50 cm each), 43 cm walls on closed arms, central platform 10x10 cm, elevated 38 cm. 5 min test immediately after OFT. Measured entries and time in open/closed arms and center, rearing, grooming, defecation, urination.

setup_habituation.evidence: Immediately after the open field test, the animal was placed in the central platform of the elevated plus-maze, facing a closed arm

setup_restrain.evidence: animal placed on central platform and observed freely

food_restriction.evidence: Animals were fasted for 12 h prior to gavage

water_restriction.evidence: no water in apparatus during test; free access in home cage

time_to_assay.evidence: The tests were performed one hour after dosing

sample_size.evidence: n =10 at each dose; fluoxetine positive control n=10

outcomes.summary: Ayahuasca and fluoxetine significantly reduced entries into closed arms; 30X ayahuasca also reduced open-arm entries. Ayahuasca-treated rats spent less time in the centre. Rearing was significantly decreased in all treated groups; grooming was decreased only in 30X.
outcomes.statistics: closed-arm entries F(3,36)=16.1, P=0.000; open-arm entries 30X P=0.028; rearing F(3,36)=17.1, P=0.000
outcomes.evidence: Ayahuasca and fluoxetine treated rats had statistically fewer entries in the closed arms than the controls in the elevated plus-maze test [F(3.36) = 16.1, P =0.000], and those from the 30X dose group also entered less in the open arms than the controls

B1_num_measures.evidence: number of entries in the open and closed arms, time spent in the open and closed arms and in the central area, and number of rearing, grooming, defecation and urination

E2_shelter.evidence: EPM closed arms are part of apparatus, not a shelter (per rubric)

E6_spatial.evidence: EPM scored as single open space per rubric

D3_recording_days.evidence: tests performed on a single day

assays.assay_description: Transparent glass tank (50.5 cm tall, 39 cm diameter), water at ~25°C, depth 30 cm. 15 min adaptation 24 h prior; 5 min test scored every 5 s for immobility, swimming, and climbing. Fluoxetine positive control (20 mg/kg i.p. at 23 h, 5 h, 1 h pre-test).

setup_habituation.evidence: rats are subjected to a 15 min swimming adaptation phase 24h prior to test initiation

setup_restrain.evidence: forced to swim in a cylinder from which they cannot escape; per rubric FST counts as restraint

food_restriction.evidence: Animals were fasted for 12 h prior to gavage

water_restriction.evidence: no drinking water accessible during test

time_to_assay.evidence: The tests were performed one hour after dosing

sample_size.evidence: n =10 at each dose; fluoxetine positive control n=10

outcomes.summary: Ayahuasca-treated rats (both 15X and 30X) showed significantly more swimming and less immobility than control and fluoxetine groups. No significant effect on climbing. Fluoxetine showed same trend but not significant.
outcomes.statistics: P<0.01 for swimming increase and immobility decrease in ayahuasca groups
outcomes.evidence: Ayahuasca-treated rats from both groups showed significantly more swimming activity and less immobility than the control and fluoxetine groups (P <0.01). No treatment had a significant effect on climbing activity.

B1_num_measures.evidence: scored every 5 s for 5 min for immobility, swimming and climbing

E2_shelter.evidence: cylinder from which they cannot escape

E8_food_water.evidence: no food or drinking water accessible

D3_recording_days.evidence: test performed on a single day (adaptation phase 24 h prior is not analysed as data)

D4_baseline.evidence: adaptation phase not scored as baseline data

D5_followup.evidence: tests performed 1 h after dosing only

judge_notes: Three behavioural assays identified, consistent across all candidates: Open Field, Elevated Plus Maze, Forced Swimming Test.
Acute toxicity 14-day observation (clinical signs, organ weights, histology) excluded as it is not a defined behavioural assay with primary behavioural outcome.
Cfos and Fluoro-Jade B neural endpoints excluded per rubric (histological/anatomical readouts; the 2-h open field exposure prior to perfusion was not analysed as behavioural data).
FST setup_restrain scored 'yes' per rubric (FST cylinder is explicitly listed as restraint), overriding gpt-oss 'no'.

Total n=40 (control + 15X + 30X + fluoxetine, 10 each) based on n=10/group statement. OFT/EPM did not use the fluoxetine group's data the same way, but the rubric specifies summing across all dose/condition groups contributing to the assay.
B1 for EPM scored 3 (7+ measures: open entries, closed entries, time open, time closed, time centre, rearing, grooming, defecation, urination).
